diffs.diff: temperature_C: datasheet reading gives 0.0625 per count, the part's model has none
diffs.evidence: MAX31820 datasheet (Operation - Measuring Temperature): "The resolution of the temperature sensor is user-configurable to 9, 10, 11, or 12 bits, corresponding to increments of 0.5°C, 0.25°C, 0.125°C, and 0.0625°C, respectively. The default resolution at power-up is 12 bits." and "The temperature data is stored as a 16-bit sign-extended two's complement number in the temperature register"; Table 1: +25.0625 °C = 0191h, -10.125 °C = FF5Eh. The model states the same scale: description '0.0625 °C at the default 12 bits' and buildNotes 'Temperature = signed 16-bit register x 0.0625 °C at 12 bits (0191h = +25.0625 °C, FF5Eh = -10.125 °C)'. The model uses sim kind 'onewire-temp' (family 40 = 28h), whose conversion is fixed in the simulator (src/sim/engine.ts owTemp: 'DS18B20 default 12-bit resolution: 0.0625 °C steps', Math.round(value*16)/16) rather than a scale field, so the gate's extractor finds no scale constant; the scale is identical at 0.0625 °C/LSB, and MicroPython's ds18x20 driver applies it in the example code.
